steps.say:
It would hold up for reads, but each server would keep its own copy.

SQLite lives in one file on one machine, so three app servers means three caches. A product page cached on one server is a miss on the other two, and when a price changes you have to clear it in three places, or a shopper sees the old price until that copy expires.

Reads themselves are fine: SQLite serves many readers at once, and a cache hit is a single indexed lookup, well under a millisecond. Writes are where it gets awkward, since only one writer holds the file at a time.

Redis is one cache all three servers share, so a page is cached once and cleared once. That is why I'd still pick it here.
